newsitem.title: USA: Cargill Inc says importing Brazilian soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Cargill Inc says importing Brazilian soybeans.

text.p: Cargill Inc on Wednesday said it was importing soybeans from Brazil for use in processing plants in the southeastern United States.
"I can confirm that it's true," said Linda Thrane, spokeswoman for Cargill.
Thrane said the company would not comment on specific terms of the deal, including tonnage, shipment dates or price.
Traders in Brazil said they heard four cargoes of soybeans, or roughly 7.2 million bushels, were sold to U.S. firms this week.
In a news release, Cargill cited tight U.S. ending soybean stocks and continued strong demand for soybean meal, oil and other products as reasons for the imports.
The U.S. Agriculture Department in May forecast ending soybean stocks at 125 million bushels, the smallest amount in 20 years.
"To carry us through this period, Cargill and other companies have turned to the global market for additional supplies," the release said.
"Cargill has contracted to import soybeans from Brazil for use in our processing plants in the southeastern United States, where the shortage is particularly acute."
Cargill said Brazil would likely have to import new crop U.S. soybeans this fall and noted the USDA expected Brazil would import 1.3 million tonnes by March.
"These 'swaps' reflect the global nature of the soybean industry," the release said.
Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures fell sharply on news of the imports.
At 1047 CDT, soybeans were down 23 to 4-3/4 cents per bushel with July off 23 at $8.37.
